targets.authors: Koellinger, P., Minniti, M., Schade, C.
targets.title: Gender differences in entrepreneurial propensity
targets.evidence_quote: To answer this research question, we replicate and extend the study by KMS with GEM data from 2011 to 2016.
targets.outcome_quote: However, our results differ from those of KMS in that the effect of the women dummy variable becomes positively sig­ nificant (and not statistically insignificant) after taking into account perceptual differences in entrepreneurial skills. This means that women would have a higher entrepreneurial propensity than men when taking into account perceptual differences. Hence, our replication results not only support the main findings of KMS but also show that their focal effect and identified mechanism have become stronger in recent years.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central perceptual explanation is supported, but authors explicitly contrast the significant positive adjusted female effect against the original null effect. Confirmation of the main mechanism is a particular comparison, not an unqualified verdict on the entire replication.

reasoning: Same models on later independent survey samples from 17 and 58 countries re-test one original paper. Original citation has no printed DOI.
